seo.title: Homeless help in London - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people who are homeless or at risk in London: council help, outreach, day centres, meals, health care, benefits, work, documents and legal advice.

notice.text: Beds, opening times and eligibility can change.
Call before travelling when possible. An outreach alert, assessment or referral does not guarantee a bed. Never pay someone who claims they can secure a council or charity place.

content.text: London services are often organised by borough. Tell the worker where you are sleeping, which borough you last lived in, whether you have children, pregnancy, disability, health needs or a pet, and whether violence makes your current place unsafe. Ask what to do tonight if no place is immediately available.

contact the housing or homelessness team at your London borough as soon as you are homeless or may lose your home within 8 weeks. If you are already sleeping outside, make a StreetLink alert as well. StreetLink sends the details to an outreach team; it is not an emergency line.
. Never post personal or sensitive information publicly.
immediate violence, serious injury, overdose, trouble breathing, loss of consciousness, fire or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark first.

yourself or someone sleeping rough. Give a precise public location, the time the person is usually there and a description. The alert goes to the local outreach team, which will try to find and assess the person. StreetLink does not itself provide accommodation.

if you are homeless now or likely to become homeless within 8 weeks. In England, councils must assess eligible applicants and may provide prevention help, emergency housing or longer-term support depending on the circumstances.
search the borough website for its emergency homelessness number. Say clearly if children, pregnancy, domestic abuse, disability or another vulnerability is involved.

urgent housing advice if you are homeless, have nowhere to sleep, face abuse or harm at home, or may lose your home. Shelter gives advice but does not allocate beds.
Shelter London services and current hours

short-term emergency accommodation during severe weather. London guidance says winter provision is activated when temperatures are forecast to reach 0°C or below; boroughs arrange local access and may also respond to extreme heat.
make a StreetLink alert and contact the borough's rough-sleeping or out-of-hours team. Ask whether SWEP is active that day. Provision is temporary and availability can change.

one-to-one homelessness assessment, housing and welfare help, breakfast and lunch, showers, toilets, laundry and clothing. It is a resource centre, not a walk-in night shelter.
Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 9am–1:30pm. Wednesday morning is a women-only space; appointments and clinics operate at other times.
food, showers, laundry, health support and help with housing and employment for people sleeping rough. Email

. The weekday day centre opens at 6am; breakfast is served from 8am and advice workers are available from 8am. Confirm current closing and shower times before travelling.
food, showers, clothing, medical access, computers, housing and benefits advice, ID help, mail collection for authorised users and job skills. Open to adults regardless of background or religion.
every day, 8:30am–1:30pm. The centre states that all services are free and operates an open-door policy.
hot meals, showers, clothing, computers, phone charging, nursing and chiropody, housing and welfare advice, employment help and referrals for immigration and substance-use support.
, phone line Monday–Friday 9am–11am. Drop-in Monday–Friday 9am–3pm; closed the first Tuesday of each month and bank holidays.
people homeless or at risk in Lewisham or Greenwich. Hot food, showers, laundry, phone, computer, internet, post, housing, benefits, employment and mental-health support are available.

people aged 16 or over who are homeless or immediately at risk. Staff assess needs and may offer housing, employment, health and coaching support or refer to another service. Crisis is not an emergency shelter.

caseworkers at partner day centres help with housing, benefits and immigration. Glass Door also operates seasonal winter night-shelter circuits in west and south-west London; call or check the website for current opening dates, referral and availability.
Glass Door — get help and current winter status

day-centre support, lunch, clothing, showers by advance booking, low-cost laundry, computers, housing and welfare advice, an NHS nurse and a mobile dentist. No referral is needed for the centre; some services require booking or have a small charge.

finding accommodation, day centres, outreach and specialist services by area and eligibility. Confirm every listing with the provider before travelling because vacancies and access rules change.

content.text: 79a Tottenham Court Road; guest entrance opposite 55 Whitfield Street, London W1T 4TD
Monday–Saturday, 10am–12 noon. Free soup and a main course; clothing and toiletries are also distributed when available.
the Soup Kitchen is an independent secular charity located in a church. Religious participation is not stated as a condition of receiving food.

adults who are homeless, vulnerably housed or need practical help; direct access, no local connection or recourse to public funds required. Food, emergency clothing, sleeping bags, toilets, charging, laptops, internet, post, support work and a warm space are provided.
Christian church and charity offering pastoral care and chaplaincy as well as practical services. It does not provide accommodation.

free breakfast from 8am, weekday showers, clean clothing, toiletries and haircuts. Advice and computer access are also available. Call
Christian mission; its published policy says services are open to all regardless of religion or origin.

hot breakfast and lunch, showers, toilets, laundry, toiletries and clothing during resource-centre access. First-time visitors are offered a one-to-one consultation so staff can plan referrals.

meals, showers, laundry and a safe place to rest during published drop-in hours, with longer-term housing, health and employment support. The charity works alongside St Martin-in-the-Fields; no religious participation is stated as an access condition.

free hot meals, showers, clothes, computers, charging and advice, every day 8:30am–1:30pm. The Manna Society describes its work as Christian care and an open-door service for anyone in need; participation in worship is not stated as required.
hot food, shower, laundry, phone, computer, internet and post during the weekday Gateway drop-in. The service is aimed at people in Lewisham and Greenwich.

urgent medical or mental-health help, advice about where to be seen and out-of-hours care. Tell the adviser if you have no fixed address, phone, transport or safe place to recover.

items.name: Registering with a GP without ID or an address

content.text: NHS guidance says a GP practice must not refuse you solely because you are homeless or lack proof of address, identification, immigration status or an NHS number. A practice can still refuse for another permitted reason, such as a closed patient list.
ask for the reason in writing and take it to a day centre, Healthwatch or another GP practice.
NHS leaflet for people without proof of address

people who are street homeless, sofa surfing or living in hostel accommodation in Tower Hamlets. You can register without ID or an address. Services include primary care, mental health, sexual health, wound care, vaccinations and drug or alcohol support.
4th floor, Soho Centre for Health, 1 Frith Street, London W1D 3HZ
a specialist GP practice for people experiencing homelessness in Westminster. Homeless-health nurses also provide open-access care in streets, hostels and day centres.
check the current contact details on the NHS page before travelling; open Monday–Friday 8am–6:30pm.
rough sleepers and people living in hostels or supported accommodation in City and Hackney. It provides normal GP care and works with housing and other services where needed.

items.name: Ace of Clubs nurse and mobile dentist

content.text: Monday and Thursday 12pm–2:30pm, first come, first served.

items.name: Universal Credit without a fixed address

content.text: people sleeping rough, sofa surfing or staying in a hostel can claim if they otherwise qualify. A trusted friend's, hostel's, day centre's or Jobcentre's address may be used with permission.
If you lack ID, internet, email, bank account or a National Insurance number:
tell the Jobcentre. Official guidance describes alternative identity checks, assisted claims and payment options.

items.name: Housing Benefit for hostel or supported accommodation

content.text: Universal Credit normally covers housing costs, but people in many hostels, refuges or supported and temporary accommodation must claim Housing Benefit from the council instead. Ask the accommodation worker and borough benefits team which claim is correct.

items.name: Jobcentre Plus and Help to Claim

content.text: Jobcentre staff can provide computer access, help establish a care-of address, arrange identity checks and adapt work-search commitments temporarily when homelessness makes them difficult. Citizens Advice Help to Claim can support a new Universal Credit claim through the first correct payment.
eligible unemployed claimants receive 50% off many London pay-as-you-go fares and can buy child-rate season tickets. Eligibility depends on benefit, age and length of unemployment.
ask your Jobcentre work coach. The discount requires both a Jobcentre Plus photocard and an Oyster card and is not automatic.
Whitechapel Mission, Manna, The Passage, The Connection, 999 Club and No. 10 publish some combination of toilets, charging, computers or internet during their opening hours.

most London borough libraries provide public computers and Wi-Fi; access, printing, charging and membership rules vary. Ask the borough for the nearest open branch. Do not leave belongings unattended.
job search, skills, housing and health support for Crisis members and people accepted after assessment. Email

items.name: Whitechapel Mission job and education support

content.text: computers, basic literacy and numeracy, word-processing practice, employment links, benefits and housing advice. Ask the advice team which services are available to a new visitor that day.
staff help with accommodation, benefits, employment and training; computers, phone and internet are available during the Gateway drop-in. The service is for people based in Lewisham or Greenwich.

items.name: Find a job and local employment programmes

content.text: the official Find a Job service and a Jobcentre work coach. Ask for help creating an email address, preparing a CV, obtaining interview clothes and explaining gaps caused by homelessness.
you can start a Universal Credit claim without knowing your National Insurance number. Check a payslip, P60, personal tax account or HMRC app; ask Jobcentre staff for help if you cannot retrieve it.
Find a lost National Insurance number

items.name: Passport applications without a home address

content.text: HM Passport Office guidance recognises homelessness and lack of documents as vulnerability factors. A third party may be able to confirm your situation and accept delivery, but contact the Passport Adviceline before applying and never use an address without permission.

Whitechapel Mission, 999 Club and Salvation Army No. 10 publish postal services for people using their centres. Universal Credit may also accept a hostel, trusted person, day centre or local Jobcentre as a care-of address.
do not put any service's address on an application until staff have agreed and explained collection rules.

free, secure storage in London for people experiencing homelessness or unsafe housing, including clothes, tents, sleeping bags, work tools and documents. Self-referrals are accepted. Call for the correct location, opening time and item limits before travelling.
housing legal aid for eligible cases, including eviction, court action and challenges to council homelessness decisions. An appointment and financial eligibility assessment are required.
free and confidential legal-aid advice for eligible housing, domestic-abuse, debt and discrimination matters. Ask for a callback if you cannot afford the call; interpreting is available.
Civil Legal Advice eligibility and contact
independent free legal help in some London boroughs on housing, benefits, employment, immigration and community-care matters. Each centre has its own catchment, appointments and capacity.
, normally Wednesday 2pm–5pm except when a drop-in clinic is held.

people in London on very low income or experiencing destitution. Praxis prioritises human-rights applications and people facing homelessness; it cannot assist with every immigration category. Monthly drop-ins have very limited first-come appointments.
Praxis current advice dates and eligibility

people who have claimed or intend to claim asylum. Advisers can explain asylum support and accommodation, report destitution or homelessness, help with accommodation problems and signpost to legal representation. The service does not itself provide legal representation.

content.text: , Monday–Friday 10am–4pm and Tuesday 6pm–8pm; closed bank holidays.

confidential safety planning, housing, legal-rights, financial, immigration and mental-health support for women in London affected by domestic or sexual abuse. Refuge addresses are confidential; referrals depend on availability.

housing-rights advice and connection to appropriate services for young people in England who are homeless or at risk. London accommodation usually requires referral through a local authority and is not guaranteed by a helpline call.

former UK service personnel who are homeless, facing homelessness or in crisis. The charity can assess immediate needs including food, clothing, safe accommodation and longer-term support. Call before attending.

government-sponsored referral pathway for veterans at risk of homelessness. It can give advice and, for those at highest risk who meet the criteria, seek suitable single-person accommodation. Self-referral is accepted.

free veterinary outreach for pets belonging to people experiencing homelessness. Outreach locations and times can change; use the official contact form or ask a day-centre or Street Storage worker for the current London session.
StreetVet is not an emergency service for animals that are not already registered. In an animal emergency, contact the last vet, PDSA, Blue Cross, RSPCA or any veterinary practice for first aid.

items.name: Tell services about a pet before travelling

content.text: many hostels cannot accept animals, while some severe-weather and specialist placements can. Tell StreetLink, the borough, shelter or day centre the species, size and any veterinary or behavioural needs before accepting a route or placement.
